safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about safe or unsafe behaviors, conditions, or practices in the workplace. In HSE, these are proactive entries made by workers or supervisors to highlight both positive and negative safety-related findings during routine activities. Such observations help identify trends, reinforce good practices, and address potential risks before they escalate.
examples: Observed all workers wearing required PPE in the welding area.
Noted a blocked emergency exit during routine safety walk.
Identified proper use of lockout/tagout procedures on pump maintenance.
Observed a forklift operator using seatbelt as required.
Noticed a spill not cleaned up in the loading dock.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are critical to report as they reveal underlying hazards or unsafe conditions that could lead to incidents if not addressed. These events are used to improve safety systems and prevent future accidents.
examples: A wrench fell from scaffolding but missed workers below.
Forklift nearly collided with a pedestrian in the warehouse.
Chemical container almost tipped over but was caught in time.
Employee slipped on wet floor but regained balance without falling.
Overhead crane load swung close to a work area but no contact occurred.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to determine root causes and prevent recurrence. This category includes accidents, injuries, spills, fires, and other adverse events.
examples: Worker suffered a laceration while using a box cutter.
Forklift struck a storage rack causing minor damage.
Oil spill occurred during transfer from tanker to storage.
Employee was exposed to chemical fumes and required medical evaluation.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short in control panel.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or unsafe condition in the workplace. In HSE, these reports are used to alert management to risks that require corrective action, such as faulty equipment, unsafe practices, or environmental dangers. Timely hazard reporting is essential for proactive risk management.
examples: Reported frayed electrical cords in the maintenance shop.
Identified missing guardrails on elevated platform.
Noted chemical storage area lacking proper ventilation.
Reported loose handrails on stairwell.
Observed oil leak near hydraulic press.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any finding related to environmental protection, compliance, or impact within the workplace. In HSE, this includes observations about waste management, emissions, spills, wildlife, or any activity that could affect air, water, or soil quality. These entries help ensure environmental standards are maintained.
